title: Gradual rollout & rollback guidelines for SDK/API features: function-calling, structured output, and streaming
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Define a repeatable, low-risk gradual rollout (canary -> phased -> global) and rollback framework specifically for SDK/API surface changes that enable function calling, structured output schemas, and streaming. This ticket owns the cross-team checklist, telemetry SLOs & regression gates, release-note templates, and an automated rollback decision flow.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented rollout runbook checked into Confluence with step-by-step canary percentages, validation scripts and owner rotations. 2) Telemetry dashboards (latency, error-rate, quality regressions) with alert rules published and reviewed. 3) Release notes template created and approved by Legal/Docs/SDK owners. 4) Two dry-run exercises completed in staging with simulated traffic. 5) Rollback automation (feature-flag toggle + traffic-split) validated with a test incident recovery within 15 minutes.
runbook_summary: Phases: Canary (1% traffic to subset of customers with feature flag), Localized expansion (5-10% with additional telemetry probes), Broad trial (25-50%), Global GA. Validation steps at each phase: smoke checks, latency p95 delta, error spike detection, token-cost variance, subjective quality tests on 200 seeded prompts. If any gate fails, triggers automated rollback and incident page with paged SRE.
telemetry_gates: Primary metrics to monitor: p95 latency (tokenized streaming path and non-streaming baseline), 5xx rate, application-level correctness regressions (eval harness pass-rate), token-cost delta per 1k tokens, streaming chunk drop rate, function-calling argument mis-parsing rate. Gates: - Block: 5xx increase > 0.5% absolute or p95 increase > 250ms sustained for 5m. - Degrade (manual review): eval pass-rate drop > 3 percentage points compared to baseline. - Soft-warning: token-cost delta > 10% without latency improvement.
docs_and_release_notes: Deliverables: single-page release notes (audience: SDK consumers, platform teams) + migration appendix explaining structured output schema changes, example SDK upgrade snippets, and guidance on streaming fallback semantics. Responsible parties: Docs (lead: Priya Nair), SDK samples (lead: Jonah Park), Legal/compliance sign-off for telemetry changes (contact: Samir Patel). Link to draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sdk-rollout-runbook (placeholder).
cross_team_tasks: PM: author runbook and coordinate dry-runs. ENG: implement feature-flag, traffic-split, enhance telemetry hooks, and provide a rollback playbook. Design: update SDK sample UX and structured output examples. Docs: publish release notes and migration guide. Solutions/SE: prepare customer-facing migration webinar and FAQ. Growth: draft comms for in-product banners and changelog. Support: create triage checklist and canned responses.
risk_mitigation: - Canary only on non-critical tenants and internal beta customers for first 72 hours. - Maintain automatic fallback to previous model variant and non-streaming path if parsing errors exceed threshold. - Keep a warm pool of legacy capacity to handle abrupt rollback traffic. - Pre-allocated SRE pager rotation during rollout windows.
dry_run_plan: 1) Week 1: Deploy to staging with 100 test clients replaying production traces; validate telemetry and rollback path. 2) Week 2: Small internal canary (10 internal teams) with feature flag. 3) Week 3: 1% external canary for low-impact customers. Each dry run must produce a short retro with checklist items and a remediation plan.
rollback_playbook: Immediate criteria: any Block gate fires OR manual decision from PM+ENG+SRE. Steps: 1) Flip feature flag to previous state (engineer on-call). 2) Reroute traffic away from new variant via traffic-split control (runtime). 3) Run health-check suite (smoke + regression prompts). 4) Open incident retro doc and schedule post-mortem within 48 hours.
communication_plan: Pre-launch: announce to beta cohort and internal channels with known limitations. During rollout: pinned Slack channel (#sdk-rollout) for live updates, daily standup with owners. Post-GA: publish release notes, changelog entry, migration guide, and record a short walkthrough video. External comms owners: Growth (Elena Meyer), Solutions (Jonah Park).
open_questions: 1) Should canary customers be chosen by region, plan tier, or API usage patterns? 2) What minimum telemetry retention window is required for gating model-quality regressions? 3) Do we need an explicit security review for streaming buffer telemetry?
